flows.period: week ending 16 September 2026 (freshest published BofA/EPFR Flow Show data, released 17 Sep 2026) -- carried forward unchanged this run; a same-week LSEG Lipper cut sharply diverges and is reported alongside rather than blended in
flows.narrative: BofA's Flow Show ('Peaks and Shovels', 17 Sep) reports the week ended 16 Sep 2026 saw +$79.3B into global equity funds (ETF-driven: +$90.8B to ETFs vs -$11.4B mutual-fund outflows), with US stocks alone pulling in +$63.8B, their first weekly inflow in 4 weeks and the largest in three months; cash/money-market funds saw their biggest outflow in 9 weeks (-$75.9B) and crypto funds their biggest outflow in 11 weeks (-$800M). This directly contradicts a same-week LSEG Lipper cut showing global equity funds posting their largest weekly OUTFLOW in nine months (-$23.21B), led by a 4th consecutive weekly US equity outflow (-$31.44B), attributed to a crude-oil-driven inflation scare pushing Treasury yields higher. Both readings are genuine, differently-sourced datasets (BofA/EPFR vs LSEG Lipper) covering overlapping but non-identical fund universes -- the same EPFR-vs-Lipper divergence flagged in the prior weekly print persists and, if anything, has widened to opposite signs this week.
